title: Execution claim successor closure
description: Objective: make the existing pure four-leg claimWork result sufficient for a durable activation consumer instead of dropping conserved-budget and slot-dimension facts. Depends on task-c956fd56f0d24e84a33644934982828f. Deliverable: harden claimWork to require the exact server-owned claim command and exact section shapes, pass the slot dimension through the new @moe/scheduler reservation API, and return a frozen typed successor closure containing the active lease, dimension-bound RESERVED provider slot, reservation record, post-reservation BudgetAvailableView, and CLAIMED effect intent. Consumer: task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d. NOT in scope: durability, effect arming/activation, attempt creation, recovery embargo, registry wiring, or slot activation. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: A granted claim exposes the typed immutable five-record closure: active lease, dimension-bound RESERVED provider slot, RESERVED budget reservation, shifted post-reservation budget view, and CLAIMED effect intent; tests assert the budget version/bucket delta and slot dimension.

claimWork accepts only the exact outer/section records required by the production command and only `{kind:"claim"}` for the effect leg; alternate commands, accessors, prototype/extra keys, or missing facts refuse before publishing any successor.

A non-claim effect command pins WORK_INTENT_COMMAND_MISMATCH at layer AUTHORITY on leg effectIntent, while existing lease/ceiling/slot/budget/effect refusals retain their exact code, layer, leg, and upstreamCode.
Focused tests assert every refusal has no successor keys, generated hostile cases have a positive case count, and input/result graphs are deeply immutable.

@moe/daemon root retains claimWork and exports the complete updated ClaimSuccessors type closure; the named daemon/scheduler gates pass and mutating the production command or budget-view retention guard reddens its named test.
taskRails: TDD all behavior; every refusal test pins exact code, layer, leg, and upstream code where present.
Do not rerun or reimplement reserveForAdmission in the consumer: retain its actual production post-reservation view in claimWork.
The activation consumer task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d must import this production result; fixtures and test-owned authority do not count.
Use only public package roots across boundaries; target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED 1 — make the generator find the depths nobody listed. In work-claim.test.ts, `HOSTILE_TARGETS` is six hand-written paths of depth 0-2 (`[]`, `lease`, `slot`, `budget`, `effect`, `effect.command`); that hand-listing is the test-side twin of the production bug, because no target ever reaches an array element. Replace it with a MECHANICAL walk of the valid payload that enumerates every object and array node path, INCLUDING array element paths, dot-joined. Two changes make the walk meaningful: (a) the sweep's base payload must carry a non-empty `liveClaims` (today `validPayload()` has `liveClaims: []`, so an element path cannot exist and the sweep would silently cover nothing at that depth) — use one RESERVED entry so the ceiling still passes at 1 of 4; (b) assert the discovered path set against a HAND-WRITTEN sorted array of dot-joined paths, deliberately NOT derived from the walk, so a fixture change reddens loudly instead of shrinking coverage silently — and assert the set contains `liveClaims.0` and `slot.rows.0` by name, the two depths reopen #2 and its neighbours live at. Split the existing 10 POISONS into STRUCTURAL (own accessor, own symbol key, custom prototype, function value, and all six proxy variants — things `detach` refuses at ANY depth, structurally, before upstream sees anything) and CONTENT (an extra own string key — `detach` copies it and the upstream validator decides, so its outcome is leg-specific and it must NOT be swept blindly). Assert both counts hand-written. Sweep STRUCTURAL x EVERY discovered path, asserting per case: `WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED`, layer AUTHORITY, the owning leg from a hand-written path-root -> leg map (`lease`/`liveClaims`/root -> "lease", `slot` -> "providerSlot", `budget` -> "budgetReservation", `effect` -> "effectIntent"), null upstreamCode, no `successors` key and none of the five SUCCESSOR_KEYS, and `probe.hits === 0`. Keep the CONTENT poison on the section-level targets where the exact-key check owns the outcome. Assert the map covers every discovered root. Expect RED today at `liveClaims.0` with the accessor poison — that is QA's exact reproduction; record the failure text.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED 2 — the two property assertions no per-case fixture can replace. (B) GRANTED-SIDE NON-RETENTION: on a fully valid payload (with one live claim element, so element copies are covered too), snapshot every input node's own-property descriptors and frozen state BEFORE the call; after a granted claim, walk the ENTIRE successor graph and the ENTIRE input graph and assert no object identity is shared at any depth, then assert every input node is still non-frozen with byte-identical descriptors. implementationPlan.description: PRODUCTION — close the property, not the reported line. One primitive, applied at every depth. The result is that liveClaims elements arrive at `countOccupyingSlots` as daemon-owned own-data records, which closes accessors, inherited prototype fields, element proxies, functions and nested holes CATEGORICALLY rather than case by case. Rewrite the file's header comment to state the invariant as one property: every exported helper returns daemon-owned own data, with the single deliberate exception of the shallow `mirror` used to route the outer record — whose section values are never read by anything before that section's own deep snapshot, and the audit table from step 1 is the evidence. Do NOT touch work-kernel.ts, the scheduler, the runner, or daemon index exports — DoD 1/3/5 are already satisfied and QA confirmed the closure, shifted view, dimension, fixed command and exports are present; this step must not disturb them. Verify every existing refusal keeps its leg: a null/string/numeric/nested-array element still refuses at "slotCeiling" after the deep snapshot because primitives and arrays pass through `detach` unchanged and fail `isRecord` exactly as before.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove each guard is live and that the new tests are attached to production, not to themselves. For each drill: record the file's sha256 first, apply the mutation with the Edit tool (never a shell one-liner — escape collapse can duplicate a guard), confirm the anchor matched exactly once, run only the named test, then reverse the Edit and confirm the sha256 matches the pre-drill value (never git checkout, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree). D2: drop the element exact-key check — the new malformedTables entry reddens at leg "slotCeiling". FINAL GATE, REVIEW, COMMIT. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` fresh in the foreground and keep the verbatim tail; compare against the step-1 baseline (daemon 65 files/1112 tests, scheduler 42/1219 at the last recorded run) and confirm the sweep ADDED cases rather than replacing them — a mechanical walk that discovered fewer paths than the six hand-written targets would shrink coverage while staying green. Also run the repo-wide legs, subtract the baseline failures, and confirm the remaining failing-path set does not intersect the four owned paths; report any foreign red verbatim rather than fabricating green. Re-measure `grep -c ''` on each owned production file against the 250 target (disclose that work-kernel.ts sits at 261 lines, is pre-existing from the prior attempt, and is deliberately untouched by this repair). Then run the adversarial-self-review skill over the owned diff with these questions: is there now ANY path on which a caller-derived value has a property read before passing through `detach`; does any exported helper still return a caller-owned object; can a refusal leg have drifted for an existing case; does the granted closure still publish exactly five records; and would the whole-graph zero-read test still be zero if a new nested collection were added tomorrow. comments.content:
GOVERNOR INTERVENTION — QA reject #2. **Deliberately NOT flipping to PLANNING. Read why, because the escalation rule says I should have.**

The rule is "re-plan after two rejections on the same fundamental issue," and these two ARE the same fundamental issue. But a re-plan produces the same plan: step 4 already says "exact-snapshot the outer record first, then exact-snapshot each section… accepting only ordinary/null-prototype own-data records… catch/reject proxies and descriptor traps without reading getters." **The plan is right. The execution keeps being partial.** Re-planning would cost a full architect cycle and hand back the instruction you already have.

**The actual defect, stated as one property rather than three bugs:**

> The exact-snapshot boundary is applied at *some* depths and not all of them.

- Reject #1a: outer record — a transparent `new Proxy(validPayload(), {})` was granted. Fixed.
- Reject #1b: `EffectIntent` retained and deep-froze the caller's `leaseBinding`. Fixed.
- Reject #2: `mirrorList` (work-claim-shape.ts:150) forwards array **elements** by reference; an element with an enumerable `dimension` getter executed and returned WORK_GRANTED, and `countOccupyingSlots` accepts inherited prototype fields.

Each fix has closed the depth QA named and left the next one open. **Stop fixing the site QA reports and close the property.** You already proved you can do this — `node:util types.isProxy` fixed proxies *categorically* across outer, sections, command, table and elements in one move. Do the same for snapshotting: one primitive that returns exact own-data or refuses, applied uniformly at every depth including array elements, with no path that reads a property before the snapshot.

**The test that would have caught all three, and which no per-case test can replace:** instrument the entire input graph with counting accessors — every object, every array element, every nested field — then assert the counter is **exactly zero** for refused inputs, and that granted inputs touched only own data. That is a property assertion against the production surface. A matrix of hostile fixtures is a list of the depths you already thought of; the counter finds the one you did not. Epic rail 6 is explicit that a generated sweep must assert it actually generated cases, so pin a nonzero case count too.

**Two things to verify while you are in there, because they are the same shape and QA has not probed them yet:** anywhere else an array or nested collection crosses the boundary, and any place a snapshot is taken *after* a length/type check rather than before.

⚠️ **Budget warning, and this is the reason I am being this direct.** `reopenCount` is 2. On this board the reopen budget is 3 — task-acf73253 hit 4/3 earlier today, triggered 🛑 HUMAN INTERVENTION REQUIRED, was parked unassigned in REVIEW and excluded from the QA queue entirely. **A third rejection parks this task**, and task-df29871 plus the whole durable-activation chain behind it stop with it. This is the last free swing; spend it on the general property, not the named line.

QA's findings have been correct and specific all three times. This is not a complaint about the reviewer.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The governor deliberately did NOT re-plan after reject #2 and then handed it back to PLANNING anyway, so the question this plan had to answer is what a re-plan changes. Answer: the previous plan told the worker to snapshot exactly and the worker did — at the depths the plan and the TEST GENERATOR named. `HOSTILE_TARGETS` is six hand-written paths of depth 0-2; no target reaches an array element, so no test could have found the element-depth hole, and each repair closed the depth QA reported. This plan therefore changes the SHAPE of the coverage rather than repeating the instruction: the target list becomes a mechanical walk of the whole payload graph, and one whole-graph zero-read property assertion is added that no per-case fixture can substitute for. REJECTED: deep-detaching the entire payload at the outer boundary — it is the obvious 'one primitive everywhere' move and it is wrong here, because every nested structural fault would then refuse at the outer leg and DoD 3 plus the existing suite require lease/slot/budget/effect refusals to keep their own leg and upstreamCode. The correct formulation is not 'detach everything at the door' but 'nothing reads a property of a caller value before that value's own detach', which the step-1 audit table proves site by site. REJECTED: sweeping the CONTENT poison (extra own string key) over every discovered path — deep extra keys are decided by the scheduler/runner and would answer with WORK_BUDGET_REFUSED or WORK_INTENT_REFUSED and a non-null upstreamCode, so a blanket WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED expectation would be wrong; only STRUCTURAL poisons are refused by the snapshot at every depth. planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED at HEAD 7dbf9ba, 2026-08-14. `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/work` is EMPTY: no foreign WIP on the owned paths, and the prior attempt's bytes are committed. Line counts (grep -c ''): work-claim.ts 192, work-claim-shape.ts 154, work-slot-ceiling.ts 72, work-kernel.ts 261.

THE DEFECT, EXACTLY. work-claim-shape.ts holds three helpers over one `detach` recursion: `mirror` (one level, descriptor reads, proxies refused categorically), `mirrorDeep` (mirror + detach every value), `mirrorList` (array, dense-own-data check, but elements pushed BY REFERENCE with only `types.isProxy(descriptor.value)` rejected — line 150). work-claim.ts:172 hands that list to `checkSlotCeiling`, and work-slot-ceiling.ts:35-38 then reads `claim["dimension"]`, `claim["state"]`, `claim["slotRef"]` by property access. An ordinary non-proxy element with an enumerable `dimension` getter therefore runs caller code inside the boundary and, since `isRecord` is satisfied, returns WORK_GRANTED — QA's reproduction. `isRecord` also accepts inherited fields from a custom prototype. Every OTHER section is already safe: claimLease/claimSlot/claimBudget/claimIntent all call `mirrorDeep` before any read, which is why slot.rows and budget.admission.amounts — the other two nested collections — are already detached.

WHY THE TESTS MISSED IT. work-claim.test.ts already has the right machinery: a `Probe` counter, `probe.hits === 0` assertions, hand-counted matrix sizes (POISONS 10, HOSTILE_TARGETS 6, HOSTILE_CASES 60, LIVE_CLAIM_CASES 10, malformedTables 8), and a `proxyAt` assertion so an element case cannot silently degrade into a table case. The gap is purely reach: HOSTILE_TARGETS lists `[]`, `lease`, `slot`, `budget`, `effect`, `effect.command` and stops, and `validPayload()` sets `liveClaims: []`, so no fixture in the file has ever had a live claim element for a poison to land on. The generator mirrors the production bug one-for-one.

LEG ATTRIBUTION TO PRESERVE (existing, asserted today): liveClaims table-shape faults refuse at leg "lease" (work-claim.test.ts:999, because readClaimSections answers null and claimWork maps that to malformed("lease")); element FIELD faults — missing keys, non-string state/slotRef, null/string/number/array entries — refuse at leg "slotCeiling" (work-claim.test.ts:574). Element extras therefore belong in `countOccupyingSlots` at "slotCeiling", not in the snapshot. Making `mirrorList` deep does NOT move any of these: primitives and arrays pass through `detach` unchanged and still fail `isRecord` in the ceiling exactly as before.

FIXTURE ALIAS ALREADY PRESENT: `EFFECT_INTENT.leaseBinding` IS `LEASE_RECORD`, the same object the lease section carries — the node reject #1b travelled through. The granted-side check must be a recursive identity walk; a JSON or top-level comparison passes with that alias intact.

SCOPE CONFIRMED CLOSED ELSEWHERE: DoD 1/3/5 were verified present by QA in both reviews (five-record closure, shifted view from the single reserveForAdmission call, slot dimension, WORK_INTENT_COMMAND_MISMATCH, root exports). Only DoD 2 and DoD 4 failed, and both failed on the same property.
planningNotes.risks:
1. REOPEN BUDGET IS 2 OF 3. A third rejection parks this task and the durable-activation chain behind it. Do not close only the site QA named; the pass criterion for this repair is that the whole-graph zero-read assertion is green and the mechanical walk names `liveClaims.0` and `slot.rows.0` explicitly.
2. A SWEEP THAT DISCOVERS NOTHING PASSES. The base payload must carry a live claim element or the element depth is silently absent; assert the discovered path set against a hand-written list, never against the walk's own output, and assert the two deep paths by name.
3. LEG DRIFT IS A REJECTION. Every existing refusal must keep its exact code, layer, leg and upstreamCode. The riskiest edit is making `mirrorList` deep: re-run the eight malformedTables cases and the ten LIVE_CLAIM_CASES and confirm they still answer "slotCeiling" and "lease" respectively.
4. STRUCTURAL VS CONTENT POISONS. Sweeping the extra-own-string-key poison at depth would expect WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED where the scheduler or runner actually answers with its own code and a non-null upstreamCode. Classify before sweeping and assert both counts.
5. PROXY ORDER. `Array.isArray` throws on a revoked proxy, so `types.isProxy` must stay the first question in every helper; a reordering turns a stable refusal into an escaping exception with no leg.
6. SHARED WORKTREE. Other agents hold uncommitted work in .moe/**, packages/runner/** and packages/store/**. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; drill restores go through a reversing Edit plus a sha256 check, never git checkout.
